newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish police probe attack on "dirty war" witness.
newsitem.headline: Spanish police probe attack on "dirty war" witness.

text.p: Spain promised on Monday to investigate the weekend abduction, torture and rape of a key witness against a Civil Guard general accused of waging a "dirty war" against Basque rebels in the 1980s.

The daily El Mundo said the witness, whose identity is kept secret for his protection, had testified against General Enrique Rodriguez Galindo, a general indicted for the kidnapping, torture and murder of two presumed Basque guerrillas during a 1980s "dirty war" on separatist ETA rebels.
Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said the report was under investigation and that the incident showed the government's witness-protection plan was not working.
"...These measures were not sufficient and it is regrettable in retrospect that more measures were not taken including some against the will of a protected witness," Oreja said.
The minister said Spain's state secretary for security and senior police officials had launched an investigation.

The ordeal of the secret witness was not the first instance of harassment of people who have come forth with "dirty war" testimony. Two members of the Civil Guard were suspended in August after being caught while they filmed another witness with a video camera hidden inside a bag.
The two Civil Guards were based at Intxaurrondo, the paramilitary force's main base in the Basque region and a fief of Galindo.

Galindo and senior officials of the former Socialist government have been accused of running death squads that killed 28 people from 1983 to 1987. Though the campaign was aimed at ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), one-third of those killed were the victims of errors and mistaken-identity murders.

Last week, the Supreme Court decided it would not question former Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez in connection with the "dirty war" even though the number two in the new conservative Popular Party government has accused him of masterminding it.
El Mundo said the witness, a former navy intelligence agent, had been abducted on Friday night in the southern Spanish town of San Fernando.
He was gagged, handcuffed, beaten, burned with cigarettes and sodomised with a blunt object, the paper said.
It quoted local police sources as saying the abductors had threatened the witness' three-year-old daughter and the rest of his family and demanded he alter his testimony against Galindo.
They told him he was talking too much and stuffed into his mouth a copy of the order declaring him a protected witness issued by Judge Javier Gomez de Liano, who is in charge of the case.
After hours of torture, he was left bound on a beach where passers-by found him in the morning.
Galindo worked in the Basque region for 26 years, almost exclusively against ETA. He has been decorated 26 times, including with the Civil Guard Gold Cross.
